source_detail: Average Effective Tariff Rate — Statutory (Yale) & Collected (Census) through October 21, 2026
title: Average Effective Tariff Rate
subtitle: Statutory (Pre-Substitution) vs. Collected Rate, through October 21, 2026
latest_source: Yale Budget Lab (statutory 11.0%); Penn Wharton / Census Bureau (collected 7.1%, Aug 2026)
methodology: TWO SERIES SHOWN: (1) 'Statutory' (navy line): Yale Budget Lab pre-substitution rate — announced tariff schedules applied at HTS10 × trading-partner level to ~20,000 product codes × ~240 partners, weighted by pre-tariff import shares. No behavioral adjustment. (2) 'Collected' (teal line): Census Bureau 'Calculated Duty' ÷ total US goods imports × 100 — the realized tariff rate reflecting actual trade flows, substitution, exemptions, and refunds. Sources: Penn Wharton Budget Model (USITC DataWeb), USAFacts, Apollo/Macrobond. The gap between the two measures the economic distortion from tariffs.

collected_series.source: US Census Bureau / Penn Wharton Budget Model
collected_series.source_detail: Census 'Calculated Duty' ÷ total US goods imports × 100 (Slok / Apollo methodology)
collected_series.methodology: Monthly customs duties actually collected (or calculated) by CBP, divided by total goods import value. Reflects trade diversion, substitution effects, exemptions, and refunds. Penn Wharton uses USITC DataWeb; Slok/Apollo uses Census Macrobond feed.
notes: Monthly collected/realized effective tariff rate from Census Bureau data (customs duties ÷ total goods imports × 100). This is the metric Torsten Slok (Apollo) uses in The Daily Spark.

Confirmed data points marked 'PWBM confirmed' come from Penn Wharton Budget Model updates citing USITC DataWeb. Interpolated points fill gaps using policy-event timing and neighboring confirmed values.

The gap between statutory (~11%) and collected (~7%) rates reflects: (a) importers shifting supply chains away from tariffed goods, (b) exemptions and exclusions actually applied at the border, (c) IEEPA duty refunds ($147B in FY2026), (d) trade simply not happening.
Net negative customs revenue months (May-Jul 2026) occurred when IEEPA refunds exceeded new duty collection, temporarily distorting the collected rate downward.

TWO SERIES: The chart shows both the Yale Budget Lab statutory rate (navy stepped line, pre-substitution) and the Census/Wharton collected rate (teal line, realized duties). The gap between them measures tariff-induced economic distortion.

Yale methodology: announced tariff schedules (MFN, Section 232, Section 301) applied at HTS10 × trading-partner level, weighted by pre-tariff import shares. No behavioral adjustment. Pipeline: github.com/Budget-Lab-Yale/tariff-rate-tracker.
Collected methodology (Slok/Apollo): Census 'Calculated Duty' ÷ total goods imports × 100. Reflects actual trade flows, substitution, exemptions, refunds.
Key 2025 events: April 'Liberation Day' (peak ~28%), US-China pause, CIT ruling, Federal Circuit stay, August reciprocal tariffs, November exemptions.
Key 2026 events: SCOTUS vacates IEEPA (Feb 20), Section 122 surcharge (Feb 24-Jul 24), Section 232 metals + pharma, Section 301 replacement (Jul 24), pharma phase-in complete (Sep 29).
Current (Oct 21, 2026): Statutory 11.0% (Yale), collected ~7.1% (Wharton, Aug data). Yale projects 11.8% by year-end. Lawsuit filed Oct 20 challenging 50% Canada tariffs under Section 338.
